service-fusion.name: Service Fusion
service-fusion.role: not stated in the API docs; the credential pages live under the admin site (admin.servicefusion.com/developerSettings), so presumably an account admin
steps: Sign in at admin.servicefusion.com.

Open https://admin.servicefusion.com/developerSettings/oauthConsumer (the OAuth Consumer page) and copy the Client ID and Client Secret generated for your user. (Docs call this the 'Client Credentials Grant'. Menu label inside the app is not stated.)

Exchange them for a token: POST https://api.servicefusion.com/oauth/access_token with JSON {"grant_type":"client_credentials","client_id":"<CLIENT_ID>","client_secret":"<CLIENT_SECRET>"}. Response has access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600 (1 hour) and refresh_token.

When the token expires, POST the same endpoint with {"grant_type":"refresh_token","refresh_token":"<REFRESH_TOKEN>"}, or repeat the client_credentials call. Rate limit 60 requests per minute per token.

Alternative (only if building a login-popup app): register an app at https://admin.servicefusion.com/developerSettings/oauthApps via 'Add New OAuth App' (Authorization Code grant). Not needed for one business reading its own data.
service-fusion.auth: Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN> (or ?access_token=<ACCESS_TOKEN> query param; do not use both). Token is short-lived (1 hour).

steps: Since Spring '26 creating new Connected Apps is restricted; Salesforce recommends External Client Apps. This is the simplest supported one-org route I found: an External Client App using the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials flow.

In Setup, open External Client Apps > External Client App Manager and create a new app (a guide says you may first need to allow creation in External Client Apps > Settings; label wording varies by release).
Enable OAuth settings, add the 'Manage user data via APIs (api)' scope, and tick 'Enable Client Credentials Flow'; accept the warning and save.
Edit Policies and choose the Run As user for the client credentials flow (Enterprise Edition: an integration user with API Only User permission). Use a read-only profile/permission set for that user.
Open the app's Settings, expand OAuth Settings/Policies, click Consumer Key and Secret (identity verification may be asked) and copy both.

Request a token: POST to the org's My Domain token endpoint (https://<MY_DOMAIN>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token) with grant_type=client_credentials and the key/secret (Basic auth header is the more secure option). The endpoint path is from general Salesforce knowledge and was not stated in the pages I could read.
